name: Public Company Comps Workbench
summary: Review 254 public companies across 12 sectors, with Capital IQ financials, trading multiples, peer-group summary statistics and comparability notes.
decision: Which public companies are genuinely comparable, and what valuation range does the reviewed peer evidence support?

sections.heading: Download the populated public-company comps
sections.html:
Download the 12-sector public-company comps workbook · Excel · 254 companies · Prices as of September 8, 2026

This is the populated workbook assembled by Claude from Mike's Capital IQ export. It includes company-level trading data, calculated multiples, peer-group summary statistics, business descriptions and comparability notes across all 12 sectors. The figures and summaries are retained from the supplied workbook.

Precedent M&A is excluded. The earlier blank template has been replaced by this populated workbook.

sections.heading: What is in the workbook
sections.html:
Trading_Comps: company names, tickers, geography, currency, market-data dates, enterprise value, LTM and NTM financials, valuation multiples, business descriptions and inclusion notes.

Peer_Group_Summary: metric-specific company counts, minimum, 25th percentile, median, 75th percentile and maximum multiples. The file contains 36 distinct peer-group labels.

Exclusions_Review: excluded or borderline names and the original review notes.

Read_Me and Sources: the original source description, dates, definitions, limitations and record references.

sections.heading: Read the snapshot on its stated basis
sections.html:
The workbook labels prices as of September 8, 2026 close, Quick Comps data as of September 9, and extraction on September 10. It is a dated snapshot, with stored values and summary statistics. Editing a company input does not recalculate the stored summaries, and the workbook does not refresh market data.

LTM and NTM coverage varies by company. Blank and NM entries remain as supplied. Some company IDs, fiscal-year ends and consensus estimates are missing. The source review notes may include earlier collection notes that were not subsequently reconciled.

Most rows are denominated in USD, with some profile-sourced GBP and CAD rows identified in the currency column. Confirm matching currencies, accounting definitions and financial periods before using a multiple. Currency-neutral ratios do not, by themselves, establish business comparability.

Preserve the distinction between reported and calculated multiples. The supplied workbook does not include the EPS inputs needed to independently reproduce its P/E figures. Its original source and usage notes remain in the download.

sections.heading: Use the peer evidence in the deal decision
sections.html:
Start with business model, revenue mix, size, growth, margins, customer exposure and geography. Use the peer-group ranges as evidence for a valuation judgment, and explain why the target should sit above, below or within the observed range.

Use the Acquisition Mandate & Target Screen to confirm why the target belongs in the search. Keep buyer-created benefits separate using the Synergy Underwriting & Value Bridge.

Carry the selected market reference into the Capital Allocation & Deal Affordability Tool and the LOI Economics & Risk Allocator. A public trading range does not establish the buyer's affordable price or private walk-away ceiling.

sections.heading: Version
sections.html: Version 1.1, September 10, 2026. Replaces the blank template with Claude's supplied 254-company workbook. Company figures and peer summaries are unchanged. The precedent M&A tab was removed and the cover's peer-group count was corrected from 37 to 36.
